newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: MRCB signs property deal with two firms.
newsitem.headline: MRCB signs property deal with two firms.

text.p: Malaysian Resources Corp Bhd (MRCB) on Wednesday signed a joint venture agreement with Fraser & Neave Holdings Bhd (F&N) and Singapore's Centrepoint Properties Ltd to develop a mixed property project in Kuala Lumpur.
MRCB holds 50 percent equity in the joint venture while F&N and Centrepoint each have 25, MRCB chairman Khalid Ahmad said at the signing ceremony.
The companies will jointly develop a retail centre, hotel apartments, corporate apartments, and an office block in the Kuala Lumpur Sentral project, at a cost of 1.1 billion ringgit.
The project cost includes 351.5 million ringgit for a 7.73-acre piece of land for the mixed development project.
Kuala Lumpur Sentral's managing director Wong Dor Loke told reporters the development will take three years to complete.

Kuala Lumpur Sentral is a 72-acre parcel located in the main railway yard of Malaysian state railway company which is being converted into a mini-city. MRCB holds a 64 percent stake in the 3-4 billion ringgit development, which includes hotels, office buildings, condominiums, a sports centre and express railway links to the new Kuala Lumpur international airport.
The project is slated for completion by 2006.

Centrepoint is the fourth foreign investor involved in the project. MRCB last August signed deals with Daito Trust Construction Co to develop a four-star hotel and another with an unnamed Japanese investor to develop a five-star hotel. In September, it signed a joint venture agreement with Singapore's Pidemco Land Ltd to build two blocks of 400-unit condominiums.
